back2basics.text: Convergence means combining the money and staff of existing schemes behind a single district plan instead of creating a new scheme. It addresses fragmentation: when irrigation, credit and storage are run by separate departments, a farmer gets one without the others and productivity does not move. The District Collector-led plan is the instrument that makes convergence enforceable.

2026-10-13-am-8ea9d14104.deck: The Cabinet has widened a convergence scheme for low-productivity farm districts. The design borrows from the Aspirational Districts Programme, so the real question is whether convergence works better than another subsidy.

structure.conclusion: Convergence works when rankings drive decisions; end on the monitoring design.
structure.intro: State the expansion and its convergence design in one line.

mcq.stem: Consider the following about the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana as expanded in October 2026: 1. Districts are selected on low productivity, moderate crop intensity and below-average credit disbursement. 2. Each district plan is prepared by a committee chaired by the State Agriculture Minister. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: The district committee is chaired by the District Collector, not a minister. The scheme is district-led by design.

body.label: Scale
body.text: The scheme now reaches 100 additional districts. The outlay of ₹11,440 crore covers the period 2025-26 to 2030-31, so it is a multi-year commitment rather than a one-season package.

body.label: Convergence, not a new subsidy
body.text: It converges 36 existing schemes across 11 departments. The money mostly flows through programmes that already exist; the scheme changes how they are planned and tracked in a district.

body.label: Beneficiaries
body.text: The release expects the scheme to benefit about 1.7 crore farmers.

body.label: Three indicators
body.text: Districts qualify on low crop productivity, moderate crop intensity and below-average credit disbursement. Each indicator points at a different bottleneck: output per hectare, how many seasons the land is cropped, and whether farmers can borrow.

body.label: Why these three together
body.text: A district can have water but no credit, or credit but poor yields. Selecting on all three targets places where the gap is structural, which is why the Cabinet framed convergence of irrigation, credit and storage as the focus.

body.label: District plan
body.text: Each district prepares a District Agriculture and Allied Activities Plan through a committee chaired by the District Collector. The Collector sits above every line department, so one officer can make 36 schemes pull in the same direction.

body.label: Monitoring
body.text: Progress is tracked monthly on a dashboard against 117 key performance indicators, and NITI Aayog reviews district rankings every quarter. A central nodal officer is assigned to each district for field visits.

body.label: Stated objectives
body.text: Post-harvest storage at the panchayat and block level, better irrigation, and access to both long-term and short-term credit.

sections.heading: How will it run inside a district?

body.label: The template
body.text: The release says the scheme is modelled on the Aspirational Districts Programme. That programme's method is to rank districts on measurable indicators and let the ranking create pressure on district administrations.

body.label: What to watch
body.text: The design depends on the ranking being honest and the dashboard being used. If the 117 indicators become a reporting exercise, convergence stays on paper; if they drive decisions, the scheme can lift productivity without a new subsidy line.
